causal_chain.bug_semantics: Scriban's object-to-string rendering recursively formats every ScriptObject member value without tracking object identity. With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer: it added the ScriptObject-specific pretty-print branch to ScriptValueConverter.ToString and the recursive call result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value)). Its parent only handled ScriptObject through the generic IEnumerable path and did not recursively extract a KeyValuePair's Value, so the advisory PoC's self-referential ScriptObject path was absent. Later commits moved/refactored the formatter; a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d added an opt-in recursion guard but explicitly initialized ObjectRecursionLimit to 0, preserving the vulnerable default rather than introducing the already-existing recursion.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The API scope middleware derives write versus read permission solely from the HTTP method and therefore treats every GET as read-only. The GET runner registration-token handlers are not read-only: shared.GetRegistrationToken calls NewRunnerToken when no active token exists and returns the usable token. A leaked read:user token (or the corresponding read-scoped owner/repository token) can consequently mint or obtain a runner registration credential, register an attacker-controlled Actions runner, and receive workflow work exposing source and repository secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable GET-plus-create design first appears in PR #27144 source member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f, which added the shared state-mutating handler and reachable organization/admin GET routes; member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 then added the user and repository GET routes. GitHub squashed the 22-member PR into mainline aggregate baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, so that aggregate is not the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 installed internal/i18n.Middleware() on the global Gin router, so every unauthenticated request supplied its raw, trimmed Accept-Language header to NewLocalizer. NewLocalizer passed that unbounded value directly to go-i18n, whose tag parsing reaches golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 guard counts '-' separators but the scanner also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB header made from malformed underscore-separated subtags bypasses the guard and exercises quadratic gobble/memmove behavior. The same unbounded parser was also reachable through X-Locale and the lang query parameter via ResolveLocale, with those explicit-locale paths potentially adding another parse. This is an unauthenticated CPU denial of service on public routes.

The underlying parser behavior pre-existed in dependencies, but Ech0's remotely reachable unbounded data path did not exist in the immediate parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated users remain inside their configured filesystem scope but can bypass administrator path deny rules because authorization compares the uncanonicalized virtual path literally while the backing filesystem resolves an equivalent name differently. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant such as /secret.TXT names denied /Secret.txt without matching its case-sensitive rule. On Windows, a mixed-separator traversal such as /allow\..\Secret.txt likewise misses the slash-based rule while filepath/afero resolves it to the denied file. The affected operations include reads and, subject to the user's ordinary permissions, modification, deletion, copying, and sharing; internally generated OS-separated paths also caused nested recursive/archive checks to miss rules on Windows.

reasoning: The report's proposed attack crosses the browser/server boundary: changing a browser request is always possible, so a bypass exists only if the Frontend API fails to bind an OTP attempt to the prepared factor and sign-in state. The public SDK at 5.88.0 passes the UI-selected factor strategy and code to that API, but contains no server-side authentication decision. Git diff shows 5.88.0 did not introduce the relevant request path, and git log -L shows the generic path existed years earlier. There is no closing patch or first patched package version; 5.89.0's OTP work only changes the input UI. Most decisively, on 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE after determining it was not a security issue, and Clerk's first-party history says it was never a real vulnerability. Selecting the 2022 request helper, the 5.88.0 release commit, or any later change as a BIC would therefore violate the protocol's requirement for the smallest commit that first wrote genuinely vulnerable lines. Since no true BIC exists, there is no parent-absence claim and no BIC commit object on which an AI marker may be judged. EVIDENCE_GAP is used rather than NOT_AI because a closed NOT_AI verdict requires a real BIC; it is used rather than BLOCKED because the repository and public lifecycle are accessible, but the reachable evidence does not establish any vulnerability to attribute.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that, after beginning an OAuth sign-in and reaching an OTP challenge, an attacker could alter the attempt request's authentication strategy (for example, swap an email-code attempt to another factor) and have the server complete authentication without the correct code. The public clerk-js 5.88.0 UI does send the factor strategy and entered code to the Frontend API, but that client-controlled request is not an authentication trust boundary; the alleged bypass requires the server to accept a strategy that was not valid for the sign-in attempt. The CNA later rejected CVE-2025-63700 because further investigation established that this was not a security issue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: No verified flaw exists in the audited repository. The allegation depended on improper state/factor validation by Clerk's non-public Frontend API backend, while clerk/javascript only constructs and sends the client request. The relevant client request behavior predates 5.88.0 and was unchanged by that release, and the authoritative CVE record plus Clerk's first-party vulnerability history state that the report was investigated, withdrawn, and never a real vulnerability.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and API key, then made server-side requests and returned the remote JSON response or selected event data. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but treated every syntactically ordinary hostname as safe without DNS resolution. A hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address therefore bypassed the guard, allowing an anonymous network caller to make cti-transmute reach an internal HTTPS service and disclose its response. The direct fix resolves domain names, requires every resulting address to be globally routable, and requires authentication on both routes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The volume-target PATCH handler authorized baremetal:volume:update, loaded the complete existing VolumeTarget, applied even an unrelated permitted patch such as one to extra, persisted it, and serialized the returned object with convert_with_links without either enforcing baremetal:volume:view_target_properties on the response or masking password-like values in properties. It declares affected ranges >=17.0.0 <29.0.6, >=30.0.0 <32.0.2, >=33.0.0 <35.0.2, and >=36.0.0 <37.0.1, and links the master and stable fixes.
